message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower from scratch would be a massive undertaking—think of a 300‑meter‑tall lattice structure with thousands of steel panels, rivets, and exposed surfaces. Even though the tower is routinely repainted every 7–10 years (to protect against rust), a full repaint from the ground up would involve:

| Task | Rough Time Estimate |
|------|---------------------|
| **Preparation** (cleaning, rust removal, surface prep) | 1–2 weeks per section, but overall ~1 month |
| **Coating application** (primer + multiple coats of paint) | 2–3 weeks per section, overall ~2–3 months |
| **Drying & curing** (allow paint to set properly) | 1–2 weeks per coat, overall ~1 month |
| **Inspection & touch‑ups** | 1–2 weeks |
| **Total** | **≈ 5–6 months** |

This assumes a dedicated crew working continuously, with weather permitting. In practice, the tower’s maintenance crews schedule repainting during off‑peak tourist seasons and use specialized equipment (like scaffolding, cranes, and spray rigs) to keep the work efficient. If you’re asking about a hypothetical “paint‑the‑tower” project, expect a multi‑month effort, not a quick weekend job!
